prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System = Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell). It is an ATFM/A-CDM layer; airports Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional and Southport keep safety authority. Parts: Demand Prediction Service (Marlinstone), Capacity Assessment Module (CAM), Slot Allocation Engine, Airport CDM Portal (Foxglove; shared workspace with Common Situation Display and departure/arrival/milestone views), Digital Briefing Room, Tower Sequence Manager, Ramp Movement Board, Departure Metering Service, Arrival Regulation Console, Contingency Operations Console, Weather Ingest Gateway (WIG, Orchard), Flight Data Exchange, Surface Surveillance Adapter, Airline Interface Adapter, Alert Distribution Hub, Performance Analytics Warehouse, Audit Event Ledger, Identity Access Service (role-scoped access), Business Rules Registry (BRR), Time Synchronization Service, Collaborative Decision Log, North/South Runway Meter, East/West Apron Sensor, Sector Load Monitor, Gate Conflict Detector. Externals (authenticated, audited): airline reservation, crew, baggage, commercial, national surveillance, avionics, airline operations centres. Actors: Regional Flow Manager (Copperfin); Airline Operations Coordinator (Saffron): FIM status, TOBT, passenger readiness, constraint notes; Ground Handling Dispatcher: servicing, baggage, staffing, equipment milestones; Ramp Control Lead: stand release, apron conflicts, tugs, pushback inputs; Tower Supervisor: vets runway configuration, sequence feasibility, tower constraints before metering; Slot Coordinator: checks CTT feasibility, logs accepted/rejected/unresolved slot adjustments in Collaborative Decision Log; Airport Duty Manager: Airport Capacity Plan, local impacts, confirms mode transitions; Meteorology Briefing Officer: attaches weather interpretation, confidence, impact timing (not authoritative); Data Governance Steward: fields, status values, retention, quality thresholds, Ledger timestamps; System Support Engineer: availability, latency, session faults, time sync. Also Network Operations Liaison, Aircraft Operator Representative, Handling Resource Planner, Deicing Coordinator, Airspace Sector Planner, Military Airspace Liaison, Emergency Response Coordinator. Items: Flight Intent Message (FIM), Airport Capacity Plan, Target Off Block Time (TOBT), Calculated Takeoff Time (CTT), Airport Acceptance Rate, Tactical Regulation Proposal, Ground Delay Program status, Storm Cell Snapshot, Runway Inspection Note, Post Operations Report, forecast confidence record, Crew Bus Delay Slip, milestone times record. Modes: Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, Recovery Phase,

Document units:
S173: After operations, the Performance Analytics Warehouse uses the recorded milestones and decision history to compare planned outcomes with actual off-block, takeoff, landing, and stand events.
S174: Tower and airport duty coordination establishes the working link between live control positions, the airport duty desk, surface surveillance feeds, and operational safety checks.
S175: The Tower Supervisor remains accountable for control tower coordination and keeps the Airport Duty Manager informed of conditions that may affect runway, taxiway, stand, or apron availability.
S176: For this section only, Brindle is the operational alias used by Tower Supervisor during voice coordination drills.
S177: The Airport Duty Manager maintains the airport duty desk as the single operational point for airport status confirmation during Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, and Recovery Phase.
S178: The duty desk reviews tower inputs, airport operations reports, and surveillance indications before confirming whether a local condition should be reflected in the Airport Capacity Plan.
S179: The Surface Surveillance Adapter consolidates position updates from the East Apron Sensor and West Apron Sensor and presents movement indications to the Airport CDM Portal.
S180: The Tower Sequence Manager uses validated surface status to support local sequencing decisions without replacing controller judgment or established radio procedures.
S181: The Airport Duty Manager uses the Runway Inspection Note to confirm that the duty desk has a current record of pavement status before endorsing any declared capacity change.
S182: Orchard shall issue time-stamped weather condition updates for use in tower and airport duty coordination.
S183: When surveillance data conflicts with tower observations, the Tower Supervisor and Airport Duty Manager agree on the operational interpretation before the condition is shared more widely.
S184: The Ramp Control Lead reviews apron movement constraints with the duty desk when stand access, pushback flow, or tug routing affects the departure plan.
S185: The Airport CDM Portal records duty desk confirmations as operational annotations linked to the relevant runway, taxiway, apron, or stand area.
S186: The Collaborative Decision Log captures the time, origin, and rationale for each local coordination decision that affects capacity or surface flow.
S187: The Time Synchronization Service shall keep tower, duty desk, surveillance, and portal event times aligned so that later review can reconstruct the sequence of events.
S188: Surface surveillance feeds are treated as advisory evidence for airport duty decisions unless the competent controller or airport authority confirms the operational effect.
